narrative: 用Cooke、K35，或者类似的老式镜头拍一张脸，画面会显得柔和过渡，而不是锐利咬合。高光会微微晕开。
对比度会降下来。背景可能会在边缘产生漩涡感，或者微微“呼吸”。
记忆感、年代感，或者把美感看得比分辨率更重要，是这套光学系统本身的任务，在任何人碰时间线之前就已经存在。当你需要为特效或纪录片式的真实感提供硬朗的边缘时，这不是合适的工具。
如果你只是想要在现代镜头上套一个褪色调色，这也不是合适的工具——那应该用胶片褪色（Filmic Faded）或者复古胶片风（Vintage）处理，而不是这支镜头。光晕溢出（Halation）可以来自胶片本身，也可以来自滤镜；老式电影镜头可能会带来类似的晕开效果，但那种漩涡感和对比度的表现，是这支镜头本身的特质。
how: 选择真正的老式镜头，或者受老式镜头启发设计的电影定焦镜头，并用足够大的光圈拍摄，才能展示出那些像差。如果这些像差本身就是重点，就不要把光圈收到让它们表现得像现代镜头一样。
让皮肤上的高光刚好亮到足以产生光晕溢出的程度。把这个和变形宽银幕的挤压效果区分开：很多老式电影镜头其实是球面镜头（Spherical）。
提示词：Vintage cine glass on [Subject], lower contrast, gentle halation, swirling edges, Cooke or K35 character, not clinical sharpness.
when: 用它来表现记忆感、年代感，或者一张不该看起来像产品目录照片的脸。不要把它当作“在现代变焦镜头上套一个褪色LUT”的同义词。
vs: 变形宽银幕镜头是一套挤压系统；有些老式镜头确实是变形宽银幕的，但这个词条主要说的是老式球面镀膜镜头。光晕溢出只是高光晕开这一个特质。
胶片褪色是一种模拟印片效果的调色；复古胶片风则是一整套年代感的处理方式。
老式电影镜头指的是拍摄用的镜头本身。
examples_film: 《大师》（The Master）和《霓裳魅影》（Phantom Thread）常常被拿来当作在脸部使用老式或有个性的镜头的例子：更柔和的咬合、温和的晕开效果，拒绝数字影像那种冷峻的边缘。把这当作关于镜头个性的语法来借鉴，而不是照搬某一张画面去逐像素匹配。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的近邻是在锐利的现代镜头画面上套一个胶片褪色调色，或者一个复古染色褪色效果。破绽是硬朗的边缘配上一个棕色LUT，或者只有颗粒感、却没有光学层面的漩涡感或光晕溢出。
解决办法：让拍摄画面本身的对比度降低，高光温和地晕开，边缘的个性来自镜头本身。

faq.q: What is vintage cine glass in film?
faq.a: 这是带有老式镀膜和像差的老式电影镜头，会降低对比度、让高光晕开，有时还会让边缘产生漩涡感。这种个性来自光学结构本身，而不仅仅是一种调色。

faq.q: Vintage Cine Glass vs Filmic Faded
faq.a: 胶片褪色是一种模拟印片效果的调色：提亮的黑位、压缩的高光。老式电影镜头则是镜头本身：镀膜、漩涡感、光学层面的晕开。你可以只有其中一个，而没有另一个。

faq.q: When should I use vintage cine glass?
faq.a: 当拍摄用的光学系统应该比现代定焦镜头更柔和时使用它：记忆感、年代感，一张不该显得冷峻精确的脸。为硬朗的特效底板拍摄时，跳过它。

faq.q: How do I prompt vintage cine glass for AI image or video?
faq.a: 写：Vintage cine glass on [Subject], lower contrast, gentle halation, swirling edges, Cooke or K35 character, not clinical sharpness。除非你也想要那些效果，否则禁止仅靠LUT实现的褪色和变形宽银幕的挤压效果。

narrative: Put a face on Cooke, K35, or similar older glass and the image rolls off instead of biting. Highlights bloom a little.
Contrast sits down. Backgrounds can swirl or breathe at the edges.
Memory, period, or beauty over resolution is the job of the optic, before anyone touches the timeline. It is the wrong tool when you need hard edges for VFX or a documentary fact.

It is also the wrong tool if you only wanted a faded grade on modern glass: that is Filmic Faded or a Vintage treatment, not this lens. Halation can be stock or a filter; vintage cine may contribute similar bloom, but the swirl and the contrast live in the glass.
how: Choose actual vintage or vintage-inspired cine primes and shoot them wide enough to show the aberrations. Do not stop down until they behave like modern glass if those aberrations are the point.
Keep skin highlights just hot enough to halate. Separate this from anamorphic squeeze: many vintage cine lenses are Spherical.
Prompt: Vintage cine glass on [Subject], lower contrast, gentle halation, swirling edges, Cooke or K35 character, not clinical sharpness.
when: Use it for memory, period, or a face that should not look like a catalog. Do not use it as a synonym for a faded LUT on a modern zoom.
vs: Anamorphic is a squeeze system; some vintage glass is anamorphic, most of this entry is about spherical old coatings. Halation is highlight bloom, one trait.
Filmic Faded is a print-emulation grade. Vintage is a whole period treatment.
Vintage cine is the taking lens.
examples_film: The Master and Phantom Thread are often cited for older or character glass on faces: lower bite, gentle bloom, a refusal of clinical digital edges. Use that as grammar for optic character, not as a still to match pixel for pixel.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a Filmic Faded grade or a Vintage dye fade on sharp modern glass. The tell is crunchy edges with a brown LUT, or grain with no optical swirl or halation.
Fix: lower contrast in the taking image, gentle highlight bloom, edge character from the lens.

faq.q: What is vintage cine glass in film?
faq.a: It is older motion-picture lenses with coatings and aberrations that lower contrast, bloom highlights, and sometimes swirl the edges. The character is optical, not only a grade.

faq.q: Vintage Cine Glass vs Filmic Faded
faq.a: Filmic faded is a print-emulation grade: lifted blacks, rolled highlights. Vintage cine is the lens: coatings, swirl, optical bloom. You can have one without the other.

faq.q: When should I use vintage cine glass?
faq.a: Use it when the taking optic should be gentler than modern primes: memory, period, a face that should not look clinical. Skip it for hard VFX plates.

faq.q: How do I prompt vintage cine glass for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Vintage cine glass on [Subject], lower contrast, gentle halation, swirling edges, Cooke or K35 character, not clinical sharpness. Forbid LUT-only fade and anamorphic squeeze unless you want those too.
